rationale: The live catalog expires 2026-07-19T20:00:00+02:00, so a refresh is due. Verification against official sources on 2026-07-16 found NO Anthropic or OpenAI model released, renamed or deprecated between 2026-07-12 and 2026-07-16: every selector in the live catalog remains valid. The refresh is therefore not a model swap; it fixes two source defects, one automation-breaking capability gap and one unbacked selector, and records availability gates that fall inside the next catalog window.
forbidden: Research must not modify Models/providers.json; this is a proposal for a separate human-approved promotion.
No volatile model ID is written into Models/profiles.json or any stable capability profile.

findings.title: Haiku may not support the effort parameter, and the resolver emits one (INFERENCE FROM OMISSION - not settled)
findings.detail: Models/profiles.json gives `fast-low-risk` effort=low; Models/providers.json lists the `haiku` selector under that profile. `resolve('anthropic-claude-code','fast-low-risk','low')` therefore returns selector=haiku + effort=low + automation_allowed=true. Official documentation states the effort parameter is not supported on Claude Haiku 4.5 (it is absent from the supported-model list; it uses extended thinking, not adaptive effort). A recommendation followed literally would emit an unsupported parameter.
findings.reproduced_locally: python tools/adaptive/resolve_capability_profile.py --provider anthropic-claude-code --profile fast-low-risk --risk low -> selector 'haiku', effort 'low'
findings.proposed_fix: DO NOT ship the code change on an argument from omission. Gate it on one cheap verification call: send model=claude-haiku-4-5 with effort=low and observe. If it returns HTTP 400 the current recommendation is INVALID (breaks runs) and resolve_capability_profile must omit effort for selectors declaring effort_support.supported=false. If the parameter is silently ignored the recommendation is merely INERT (misleading, harmless) and a catalog note suffices. The fix differs by outcome; the catalog's effort_support block is authored either way but is only ENFORCED after the call.
findings.verifier_note: The independent verifier confirmed the effort level set is exactly low|medium|high|xhigh|max ('the values documented on this page are the complete set the API accepts') and that Haiku 4.5 is ABSENT from the affirmative supported-model list. But the page NEVER states Haiku is unsupported and documents no error behaviour: the claim rests on an argument from omission. It is stated more firmly in the original research than the source supports.
findings.blocked_on: one verification call (owner-approved); until then this finding is advisory and no code changes

findings.title: Both openai-codex official_sources are stale (308 redirects)
findings.detail: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models and https://developers.openai.com/codex/models both now 308-redirect to learn.chatgpt.com. The catalog's own discovery contract points at redirecting URLs.

findings.title: `current-frontier-creative` has no official backing on OpenAI
findings.detail: OpenAI publishes no creative-tier model. The selector's only honest resolution today is the frontier coding model (gpt-5.6-sol), i.e. it silently duplicates `current-frontier-coding` while implying a distinct capability. The `creative-design` profile would resolve to a selector whose distinctness is unverified.
findings.proposed_fix: Either (a) remove the selector and let `creative-design` be unsatisfiable on openai-codex (resolve already raises 'no current selector satisfies the capability profile'), or (b) keep it with an explicit `aliases_of: current-frontier-coding` + `distinctness: unverified` note. Recommendation: (b), because (a) silently loses provider coverage; the owner decides.

findings.title: Availability gates that bite inside the next catalog window
findings.detail: Fable 5 is unavailable under zero data retention (requires 30-day retention). Claude Code version gates: Fable 5 >= v2.1.170, Sonnet 5 >= v2.1.197, Opus 4.8 >= v2.1.154. Alias resolution is provider-dependent: on the Anthropic API `opus`->Opus 4.8 and `sonnet`->Sonnet 5, but on Bedrock/Google Vertex `sonnet`->Sonnet 4.5 and on Foundry `opus`->Opus 4.6 - so a 'provider-current-alias' means different models on different platforms. Fast mode for claude-opus-4-7 is deprecated and `speed:"fast"` errors after 2026-07-24, inside the proposed window.
findings.proposed_fix: Record gates per selector as machine-readable `availability_gates`; keep them advisory (documented, surfaced) rather than enforced, until an eval proves enforcement is safe.

findings.title: Codex effort levels contradict across two official pages
findings.detail: learn.chatgpt.com config-reference states model_reasoning_effort accepts exactly minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh; learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models shows a six-item interactive selector including Max and Ultra. Neither page reconciles them. Most defensible reading: xhigh is the config-file ceiling; Max/Ultra are CLI-surface controls (mirroring Anthropic documenting `ultracode` as NOT an API effort level).
findings.proposed_fix: Encode ONLY the config-file enum (minimal..xhigh). Record the contradiction; do not encode Max/Ultra as config values. Re-check next week.
